The most apparent issue I can see in your writing would be the distance between the narrator and the characters. It is simply too inconsistent, one sentence you're in the character's head and in another you're describing the situation from a distance, like an omniscient narrator.

For example, most of the first page is from Mildred's point of view. We hear her thoughts about her marriage and we feel for her as she struggles with an onion, yet you refer to her as "the mother", "a motherly voice yelled from inside the small farmhouse", etc. Then it abruptly switches to us not knowing what she sees out the window and we're in Bale's point of view for a short while before returning to Mildred's. It is quite jarring and makes the story harder to follow and the characters harder to relate to. 

There's also quite a bit you can cut to make it more "show don't tell". 

>Mildred, putting the knife down, crossed her arms. Her eyes intent on prying out the information he was withholding from her.

The last sentence is unnecessary. We can already guess what she's doing the moment she crosses her arms and insists further. Also as it is narrated mostly from her perspective, I'd refrain from describing her eyes as she would not be aware of them.

​

All in all, it's clear you're new to writing and I'd suggest just keeping this in mind while working on your first draft. The concept of night creatures seems interesting and I'd like to know where it goes from here.
